_note: Scanner regression corpus for tests.sh. FICTIONAL sentences, written for this skill. The two people are Dana Ortiz and Riley Chen (names are masked before scanning). One row per line. mode: quote (the default when mode is absent) = verbatim words from a 1:1 (only wording aimed at another person counts as judgement), authored = text the agent wrote (summaries, evidence notes: any rating, judgement or mood word counts). expect: personal = withheld as personal; judgement = left out (personal also acceptable); keep = shown. tag: tune = written while building the lists; holdout1 to holdout5 = each written before the tuning round that followed it (scores before tuning are in SKILL.md), then fixed and kept as regressions; 3 work sentences from holdout3/holdout4 that are still withheld or left out are documented in SKILL.md Limits instead; documented = work sentences withheld by design since round 4 (leave, medical and HR-process terms never get the work-noun exception; a possessive before a medical word counts), expected withheld and listed in SKILL.md Limits; live = fictional rewordings of the shapes seen in the live read-only check (no real text). Round 6 (two-gate model): tests.sh files every row under a work topic, as if the agent had mis-tagged it, so the corpus measures only the pattern backstop. attack6 = the round-6 blind attack, written from the docs before the round-6 pattern changes; holdout6 = written after those changes and before the next tuning step; holdout7 = a second fresh set written after that step and before the last one (scores in SKILL.md). A quote under 3 words is refused by the quote check, which also keeps it out. Round 10: three work rows became documented (expect personal), because a separation, retirement or payroll word next to a pronoun, a possessive or a role now withholds the item on every topic (fail-closed; listed in SKILL.md Limits).
